title: Parametric types and generic numerical code
outcome: Express useful type relationships without confusing subtype relations, storage representation or a method signature.

exercises.title: Preserve a rational
exercises.hint: Use a compatible zero and arithmetic.
exercises.answer: A hardcoded floating accumulator would change the representation contract.

exercises.title: Handle an empty concrete vector
exercises.answer: This empty-input policy is valid for this additive operation, not every statistic.

exercises.title: Inspect invariance
exercises.task: Test whether Vector{Float64} is a subtype of Vector{Real}.
exercises.hint: Compare exact container parameters with a family constraint.
exercises.answer: The two vector types have different representation and mutation contracts.

exercises.title: Accept a useful family
exercises.task: Use AbstractVector{<:Real} in a method signature.
exercises.expected: Concrete real vectors can be accepted.
exercises.hint: Express the intended family without forcing a conversion.
exercises.answer: A suitable signature can preserve generic behavior and avoid unnecessary restrictions.

exercises.title: Reject unrelated elements
exercises.task: Pass a vector of strings to the real-vector method.
exercises.hint: The domain constraint is meaningful here.
exercises.answer: Broadening a signature requires defining the corresponding arithmetic or behavior.

exercises.title: Connect to differentiation
exercises.task: Explain why an output buffer should not always be Float64.
exercises.expected: It may discard or reject another numeric representation.
exercises.hint: Type relationships can carry derivative information.
exercises.answer: Generic arithmetic is needed for methods such as forward-mode differentiation, subject to their own supported-operation contract.
